nodes.name: Lemma 4.20: Splitting $\exists$
nodes.statement:
If $\vdash \exists x. P \parr Q$, then there exist formulae $V_i$ and values $v_i$ such that $\vdash P\mathclose{\left\{^{v_i}\!/\!_{x}\right\}} \parr V_i$, where $1 \leq i \leq n$, and $n$-ary killing context $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ such that $\vcenter{\infer{Q}{ \mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ V_1, V_2, \hdots, V_n\ \right\}}}$
and if $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ binds $y$ then $y\mathrel{\#}\left(\exists x . P\right)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.2: Splitting $\forall$
nodes.statement:
If $\vdash \mathopen{\mathcal{C}}\left\{\  \forall x. P \ \right\}$ holds
 then, for all terms~$v$, $\vdash \mathopen{\mathcal{C}}\left\{\  P\mathclose{\left\{^{v}\!/\!_{x}\right\}} \ \right\}$ holds.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.19: Splitting $\mathrm{new}, \mathrm{wen}, \otimes, \triangleleft, \with$
nodes.statement:
The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}

\item If $\vdash \left( P \otimes  Q \right) \parr R$, then there exist formulae $V_i$ and $W_i$ such that $\vdash P \parr V_i$ and $\vdash Q \parr W_i$, where $1 \leq i \leq n$, and $n$-ary killing context $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ such that $\vcenter{\infer{R}{\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ V_1 \parr W_1, V_2 \parr W_2, \hdots, V_n \parr W_n\ \right\}}}$
and if $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ binds $x$ then $x\mathrel{\#}\left(P \otimes Q\right)$.

\item If $\vdash \left( P \triangleleft Q \right) \parr R$, then there exist formulae $V_i$ and $W_i$ such that $\vdash P \parr V_i$ and $\vdash Q \parr W_i$, where $1 \leq i \leq n$, and $n$-ary killing context $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ such that $\vcenter{\infer{R}{\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ V_1 \triangleleft W_1, V_2 \triangleleft W_2, \hdots, V_n \triangleleft W_n\ \right\}}}$
and if $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ binds $x$ then $x\mathrel{\#}\left(P \triangleleft Q\right)$.

\item If $\vdash \mathrm{new} x. P \parr Q$, then there exist formulae $V$ and $W$
where $x\mathrel{\#}V$ and $\vdash P \parr W$ and either $V = W$ or $V = \mathrm{wen} x .W$,
such that there is a derivation $\vcenter{\infer{Q}{V}}$.

\item If $\vdash \mathrm{wen} x. P \parr Q$, then there exist formulae $V$ and $W$ where $x\mathrel{\#}V$ and $\vdash P \parr W$ and either $V = W$ or $V = \mathrm{new} x. W$, such that there is a derivation $\vcenter{\infer{Q}{V}}$.

\item If $\vdash \left( P \with Q \right) \parr R$, then $\vdash P \parr R$ and $\vdash Q \parr R$.
\end{enumerate}

Furthermore, for all $1 \leq i \leq n$, in the first two cases the size of the proofs

of ${P \parr V_i}$ and ${Q \parr W_i}$ are strictly bounded above by the size of the proofs of ${ \left( P \otimes Q \right) \parr R}$ and ${ \left( P \triangleleft Q \right) \parr R }$.
In the third and fourth cases, the size of the proof ${P \parr W}$ is strictly bounded above by the size of the proofs of $\mathrm{new} x .P \parr Q$ and $\mathrm{wen} x. P \parr Q$.
The size of a proof is measured according to Definition~4.15.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.21: Splitting $\oplus$
nodes.statement:
If $\vdash \left( P \oplus Q \right) \parr R$, then there exist formulae $W_i$ such that either $\vdash P \parr W_i$ or $\vdash Q \parr W_i$ where $1 \leq i \leq n$, and $n$-ary killing context $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ such that $\vcenter{\infer{R}{\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ W_1, W_2, \hdots, W_n\ \right\}}}$
and if $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ binds $x$ then $x\mathrel{\#}\left(P \oplus Q\right)$.

nodes.statement: Section: Context Reduction and the Admissibility of Co-rules

nodes.name: Lemma 4.22: Splitting $\alpha, \overline{\alpha}$
nodes.statement:
The following statements hold, for any atom $\alpha$, where if $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ binds $x$ then $x\mathrel{\#}\alpha$.
\begin{itemize}
\item If $\vdash \overline{\alpha} \parr Q$, then there exist $n$-ary killing context $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ such that 
$\vcenter{\infer{Q}{\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \alpha, \alpha, \hdots, \alpha\ \right\}}}$.

\item If $\vdash \alpha \parr Q$, then there exist $n$-ary killing context $\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \ \right\}$ such that 
$\vcenter{\infer{Q}{\mathopen{\mathcal{K}}\left\{\ \overline{\alpha}, \overline{\alpha}, \hdots, \overline{\alpha}\ \right\}}}$.
\end{itemize}
